newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rebels said bracing for army offensive.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rebels said bracing for army offensive.

text.p: Sri Lanka's Tamil Tiger rebels are redeploying fighting units and stepping up training in anticipation of a long-awaited military offensive, military officials said on Tuesday.

Rebel area leaders in the Indian Ocean island's eastern Batticaloa district have moved to their Mullaithivu base on the northeast coast along with 300 fighters, the military officials said, citing intelligence reports.
"Up to 3,500 cadres are undergoing training in Mullaithivu preparing for an army offensive," a military official said.

Mullaithivu, 280 km (175 miles) northeast of Colombo, is the main jungle base of the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels, who are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the mainly Sinhalese island's north and east.
The military is believed to be preparing for an offensive to open a land route linking Vavuniya, 220 km (140 miles) north of Colombo, with the Jaffna peninsula, about 100 km (60 miles) further north.

The military now relies entirely on air and sea transport to send troops and supplies to bases in Jaffna, because most of the northcentral Wanni mainland region, north of Vavuniya, is under rebel control.

But the air force has lost a number of transport aircraft in recent months, mostly in unexplained accidents, while the rebel Sea Tiger naval wing has emerged as a formidable threat to naval convoys sailing to Jaffna.
The Tigers launched an artillery attack on the Vavuniya airbase on Sunday in what was seen as an effort to disrupt preparations for an offensive.
Residents from the rebel-held Wanni region arriving in Vavuniya have reported that the guerrillas were digging bunkers and building other strongpoints in preparation for an offensive.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The Tigers say the death toll is higher.
